Your operating profile

The Enthusiastic Innovator

7w8ENFPCreatorQuick Start

You run on possibility. Where other people see a closed door, you see five more that nobody has tried yet, and your instinct is to bring people with you toward them. That energy is genuinely rare. It opens rooms, starts movements, and makes hard things feel like a reasonable Tuesday. Your real work is learning when to let one of those open doors become the only door.

A guide to working with me

Working with Alex

A joyful explorer of ideas, wired to spark, connect, and create. Read this before our next one on one, or any moment where my speed, silence, or push-back is getting in the way.

ENFP7w8CreatorQuick StartSecure
What people miss

I read like a high-energy extrovert, but I am more introverted than I look. I recharge alone, prefer deep one on ones, and need quiet to do my best thinking.

When you work with me

Get to the point, and bring a recommendation.

Short is gold. I want context, but brief. Tell me what you think first.

Mornings are sharpest.

Before 9am is for deep work. Movement helps me think, so walks, coffees, and changing venues are real tools. Let's use them.

Reach me through the right channel.

Email gets checked a few times a day. Anything a day or more out, route through my assistant. Urgent, text. Really urgent, call.

Feedback is welcome.

Open with "are you open to some feedback?" That phrase lowers my guard. Acknowledgement matters too, even when I act like it doesn't.

If I am going on and on, interrupt me.

I am probably just excited and thinking out loud. You can pull me back.

When I am away, I truly unplug.

The more I disconnect, the better I come back. Some of my best ideas show up when I am out.

How I decide, and how trust works

I can decide on the spot, but I am best after a beat.

I may have strong opinions, but I am rarely attached. Push back, I am listening.

Trust is earned by doing the work.

Show me you have thought it through and stayed open. It is lost by denying or blaming, and easy to repair if you open up. I care about the learning, not the mistake.

If you notice this, it might just mean this
If I am going on and onI am excited and thinking out loud. Interrupt me.
If I go quietI am listening hard or processing. Ask me what I am thinking.
If I commit too fastAsk what I am saying yes to, and what that means I am saying no to.
If I push back hardIt is because I care, not because I am fighting.
If I miss a follow-upIt almost never means I do not care. Just nudge me.
Permission slips, please use these

You can interrupt me if I am going on and on. Try: "Sounds like you are excited. Do you want to be in brainstorming mode, or what is best here?"

You can say no to me once you have heard me out and have a strong, well-considered view.

You can tell me almost anything that helps you get what you need. Try: "I do not feel like you are hearing me. Are you open right now, or should we try another time?"

You can call or text me anytime. When I do not want to be disturbed, I turn my phone off.

In one line

Bring me a clear ask and a recommendation, meet me with candor, and don't take my speed personally. We will go further than you imagined, together.

Learnings and next moves
1

The blind spot is real, and friendly.

Your team experiences your enthusiasm as occasionally crowding them, not as a character flaw. The fix is a 10-second pause and a question ("what are you seeing?"), not a personality overhaul.

2

Tell them what they cannot see.

Your introvert side, your morning ritual, your true unplug. These are hidden assets. Share them through your guide and in one-on-ones, and trust deepens fast.

3

Acknowledgement is low cost, high leverage.

Three of five wish for more from you. A weekly "I noticed ___" for each direct report would close most of this gap.

The takeaway

This is what it looks like to grow faster than the company. The blind spots are small, the alignment is real, and the frontier is where the next chapter lives.

Where you click and where you grind
Your move with Dana

Before your next big decision, send Dana your thinking a day early. Let them process in private before you ask for a yes in the room. You will get a faster yes, not a slower one.

Scripts for the two of you

Ready-made lines that fit how Dana hears things. Steal them.

When you need a yes soon

"Not asking you to decide now, just flagging it is coming. Numbers tonight, talk tomorrow?"

When you disagree

"Help me see what I am missing. I would rather be right than fast on this one."

When you hand something off

"This is yours now. Ping me only if you hit a wall, I will not hover."

When you moved too fast

"I jumped ahead. Walk me back to where I lost you."

Rituals worth keeping

Small standing habits that keep this pair smooth.

Decisions go async-first

Send Dana your thinking a day before you need a yes. She arrives ready, you get a faster answer.

Default to written for anything with stakes

Dana trusts what she can examine. A two-line doc beats a hallway pitch every time.

Leave the last word open

End the hard ones with "sit with it, tell me tomorrow." The pause is a feature for her, not a stall.

Fast Start guide for your new hire

A 90-day plan for integrating a new teammate, built from how they are wired against the room they are joining. Draft copy below, pending Mark's onboarding pass.

First week

Draft: pair them with the person whose wiring most complements theirs. Set one clear early win. Name the team's working norms out loud.

First month

Draft: introduce the dyads that will matter most, and where the predictable friction sits. Give them their Working With Me guide and collect the team's.

First 90 days

Draft: a check-in on fit against the Talent Fit read, the gaps they were hired to fill, and one honest conversation about how it is actually going.
